title: Focused on Digital Shares Over Tokens: Cunningham
summary:
Stacey Cunningham, president of Bullish and former president of the New York Stock Exchange, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” They discuss her recent move to Bullish, market volatility, and her preference of digital shares of tokens.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Planting Bug Released on Bond
summary: A federal magistrate judge ordered that the OpenAI staffer charged with bugging a company office conference room be released on a $1 million bond, finding that prosecutors have not presented enough evidence of wrongdoing to keep him in custody.

title: Bitcoin Sinks Below $60,000 Amid ETF Outflows
summary: Bloomberg Intelligence’s James Seyffart joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” Bitcoin is set to have its eighth straight week of losses, which would be the longest weekly losing streak since 2022. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Huang to Testify Publicly Before Senators Dec. 3
summary: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Dave Lee said despite Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, questions remain about the national security risks posed by the Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese Spy and that he hopes lawmakers focus more on where Nvidia chips were sent and what Huang knew, and less on Huang's interpersonal affairs.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Kalshi Eyes Under-21 Ban to Avoid NY Shutdown
summary:
Yesha Yadav, associate dean and professor of law at Vanderbilt Law School, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” Kalshi told a judge it’s open to excluding New York users under 21 during a court hearing Monday over whether the platform should be shut down in one of its busiest markets.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bitcoin a ‘Struggle’ Right Now: Kiani
summary:
Ayesha Kiani, COO of Monarq Asset Management, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” Bitcoin is set to have its eighth straight week of losses, which would be the longest weekly losing streak since 2022.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: New Venue Fast, More Efficient: Andrew Cuomo
summary: Andrew Cuomo, former governor of New York and co-chair of OKXICE, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” They discuss OKXICE’s launch of the tokenized securities venue from the joint venture between OKX and the Intercontinental Exchange. The platform has over 100 assets available in a phased rollout for round-the-clock trading. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Expect Fundraising To Be Off Significantly: Bain's Harris
summary: Bloomberg Intelligence’s Dushyant Shahrawat and Matt Harris, partner at Bain Capital Ventures, join Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” They discuss venture capital connected to the digital asset industry. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Most Exciting Time For Fintech: Cunningham
summary:
Stacey Cunningham, president of Bullish and former president of the New York Stock Exchange, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” They discuss her recent move to Bullish, market volatility, and her preference of digital shares of tokens.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump's Nvidia Push is 'Crony Capitalism,' Says Rep.-Elect Killin
summary:
Trump's Nvidia Push is 'Crony Capitalism,' Says Rep.-Elect Killin 

Democrat Representative-Elect from Colorado Jessica Killin said that Trump's involvement in reinstating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is 'crony capitalism' and should be investigated for both potential national security risks and corruption from the president and his family. Killin also called for a 'complete overhaul' of the ethics system within congress to address corruption and restore the public's faith in government.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia Is a ‘Good Corporate Citizen,’ Attorney General Says
summary: US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Nvidia Corp. is “a good corporate citizen,” while declining to directly answer questions about whether the Justice Department is scrutinizing the circumstances that led to the temporary exit of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Staff in Employee Meeting
summary: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang apologized to employees for the conduct that led to his brief ouster, telling staff at an all-hands meeting on Tuesday that he had let them down, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: CoreWeave Bonds Hit All-Time Lows, Erasing Nvidia-Fueled Gains
summary: Bonds backing cloud computing provider CoreWeave Inc. fell to record lows Tuesday, among the day’s biggest corporate bond losses, amid renewed concerns about the durability of the AI trade.

title: Tech Slides as Nvidia, AI Risks Take Center Stage
summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at the tech selloff dragging down US stocks over AI safety fears and concerns from fresh US tariffs. Plus, what Jensen Huang's comeback as CEO of Nvidia means for the company's future as he is slated to testify before Congress next week, and HPE CEO Antonio Neri joins to discuss the company's earnings results and the impact from the Nvidia debacle on AI demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia Bull Says Huang’s Return Restores Tech Leadership
summary: StoneX senior semiconductor research analyst Cody Acree upgraded Nvidia to Buy with a $270 price target following Jensen Huang’s return as CEO, saying his reinstatement removes key uncertainties around Nvidia’s technology roadmap, industry relationships and support for the AI buildout. Acree discusses why he sees Huang’s leadership as critical to the investment case with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nvidia's Huang to Face Bipartisan Scrutiny on Capitol Hill
summary: Newly reinstated Nvidia Corp. chief executive officer Jensen Huang will testify publicly before a powerful Senate committee on Dec. 3, according to a statement from the panel’s chairman. Bloomberg's Nathan Dean joins to discuss how Trump's push to reinstate Huang could effect the upcoming hearings. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic Dips Below IPO Price in Sharp Tech Reversal
summary: Anthropic PBC shares sank 8% below their $83 initial public offering price, wiping out gains for investors who piled into the artificial intelligence lab’s record-setting debut last week. Bloomberg's Carmen Reinicke joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: HPE Forecast Trails Top Estimates, Shares Fall on AI Growth Outlook
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. shares dropped the most in more than six years after investors feared that continuing component costs will cut into the hardware company’s profitability next year despite rising revenue.

title: Nvidia Board Faces Growing Scrutiny, Trade Fears Return
summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Stocks slide as the Nvidia euphoria fades and trade fears return. Nvidia is still at the center of the storm. Cleo Capital’s Sarah Kunst says board members should resign, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi raises national security concerns, and Harvard’s Jesse Fried weighs the board’s duty to shareholders. Plus, Matt Maley on cracks in the AI trade, Anthropic falls below its IPO price, and retailers deliver a bright spot. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: HPE Customers Did Not Change Behavior Due to Nvidia, CEO Neri Says
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise gave a revenue forecast that fell short of estimates, but Chief Executive Officer Antonio Neri is still bullish and says free cash flow for shareholders will keep growing. Neri also says customers did not change their behavior due to the Nvidia drama involving CEO Jensen Huang. Neri speaks on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)
